translations.text: The oracle that the prophet Habakkuk saw.
How long, Lord, shall I cry out and you will not hear? Shall I call to you when oppressed, and you will not save?
Why have you shown me hardship and toil, making me see misery and ungodliness? Judgment took place before me, and the judge was taking bribes.
Therefore the laws have been scattered, and justice is never carried out. Because the ungodly overpower the righteous, judgment comes out crooked.
Look, you contemptuous people, and consider! Be utterly astonished and perish, for I am doing a work in your days that you will not believe, even if someone tells you.
For behold, I am rousing the Chaldeans, the bitter and swift nation that travels across the breadth of the earth to possess dwellings that are not its own.
He is fearsome and renowned, and his judgment will come from himself, and his dignity will proceed from himself.
Their horses will run faster than leopards, swifter than the wolves of Arabia. His armed men will raid and advance from far away, swooping like eagles eagerly upon their food.
Destruction will come upon the ungodly who have turned to confront them face-to-face; he will gather captives like sand.
He will make sport of kings, and rulers will be his playthings. He will mock every stronghold, heap up mounds of earth, and capture it.
Then his mind will change; he will pass on and be pleased: “This is the power of my God.”
Are you not from the beginning, Lord our God? Let us not die! Lord, you appointed him for judgment, and you created me to rebuke his mockery.
Your eye is too holy to see evil, and you cannot look upon hardship. Why did you look upon the contemptuous and remain silent when the ungodly swallowed up the righteous?
And you will make people like the fish of the sea, like creeping creatures that have no leader.
He hauled them all up with a hook, dragged them in with his net, and gathered them with his fishing nets. Therefore he will rejoice, and his heart will exult.
And for this reason he will sacrifice to his fishing net and burn incense to his net, because through them he has made his portion rich and his food choice.
Will he therefore spread his net and continually slaughter nations without sparing them?
I will stand at my watch and climb onto a rock. I will keep watch to see what he will say to me and what answer he will give to my rebuke.
The Lord answered me and said, “Write this vision clearly on tablets, so that whoever reads may read confidently.”
For the vision is still for an appointed time, and it will dawn at the end, and not in vain. But if he delays, wait for him, for the one who is to come will come and will not delay.
And if anyone wavers, my soul will take no pleasure in him, for the righteous person will live by faith.

But the conceited and contemptuous man is arrogant and will accomplish nothing. He has made himself as vast as Hades and become insatiable like death. He will gather all the Gentiles to himself and bring all nations together to himself.
Will not all these people tell a proverb about him, put him into a song, and say, “Woe to the one who piles up for himself what is not his! How long will he weigh down his yoke with heavy loads?”
For his devourers will suddenly rise, and those who plot against him will awake, and you will become their plunder.
Because you plundered many nations, all the peoples who remain will plunder you, because of human bloodshed and the ungodliness committed against the land, the city, and all its inhabitants.
Woe to the one who greedily seeks evil gain for his house, setting his nest on high to escape from the hands of the wicked!
You have devised shame for your house; you have destroyed many nations, and your soul has sinned.
For a stone from the foundation will cry out, and a worm from the wood will proclaim this.
Woe to the one who builds a city with blood and establishes a city with injustice!
Is not all this from the Lord Almighty? Many peoples dwindled because of fire, and many nations were diminished.
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord’s glory, like the abundant waters that cover the seas.
Woe to the one who gives his neighbor murky enticements to drink and makes him drunk so that he may look into their caves!
Drink your fill of dishonor instead of glory, you too; be shaken and tremble. The cup of the Lord’s right hand has surrounded you, and dishonor has gathered upon your glory.
For the wickedness of Lebanon will cover you, and the misery of the wild beasts will terrify you, because of human bloodshed and the wickedness of the land, the city, and all its inhabitants.
What use is a carved image, since they carved it and fashioned it into a cast image, a false apparition? For its maker trusted in his own creation, making useless idols for himself.
Woe to the one who says to wood, “Rouse yourself and wake up,” and to stone, “Rise up!” It is a spectacle before the eyes, wrought in silver and gold, and there is no breath at all in them.
But the Lord is in his holy temple, and all the earth will fear before him.
A prayer of the prophet Habakkuk, in song.

Lord, I heard the report of you and was afraid. Lord, I looked upon your works and was terrified. You will be known between two living creatures; when the years draw near, you will be revealed; when the time arrives, you will appear. When my soul is troubled, in anger remember mercy.
God will come from Teman, and the Holy One from the shaded, densely wooded mountain. Pause. His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was filled with his praise.
His rays will be like light, and horns will be in his hand; he established the mighty love of his power.
A word will go before his face and go out into the plains behind him.
He stood, and the earth shook; he looked, and the nations melted away. The mountains were shattered by force, and the everlasting hills melted away. I saw his everlasting ways in place of labors.
The tents of the Ethiopians were terrified, and the tents of the land of Midian.
Will the Lord be angry with the rivers? Is your wrath against the rivers, or your assault against the sea, that you mount your horses? Your riding is salvation.
You will stretch your bow tight against authority, says the Lord. The earth was split by rivers.
The nations will see you and suffer anguish, you who scatter the flowing waters. The depths gave forth their voices, their towering fury.
The sun rose, and the moon stood in its place. Your arrows will go forth in light, in the gleam of your flashing weapons.
With threats you diminished the earth, and in anger you will bring the nations down.
You went out for the salvation of your people, to save your anointed ones. You cast death upon the heads of the lawless; you roused the bonds up to their necks completely. Pause.
You shattered the heads of tyrants with astonishment. They will tremble at it; they will loosen their bridles like a poor man who eats in secret.
You brought your horses into the sea to muddy the abundant waters.

I took heed, and my heart was terrified at the sound of the prayers of my lips. Trembling entered my bones, and my belly was troubled within. I will rest on the day of distress, when I go up to the people of my exile.

For the fig tree will not give its fruit, and let there be no produce from the vine. The yield of the olive tree will fail, and let the fields produce no food. The flocks will disappear from the pasture, and there will be no oxen in the stalls.
But I will rejoice in the Lord and be glad in God my Savior.
The Lord God is my strength, and he will establish my feet to the end and raise me to the heights to triumph with his song.
